editorial:
Imagine spending your entire life with one person, sharing a love for music and art, only to have everything change in a split second. You meet Georges and Anne, a retired couple who have a very sweet and quiet life together. They are kind and smart, but their world shrinks when Anne has a stroke. Suddenly, their home turns into a place of struggle. You will feel the weight of their situation as Georges tries his best to take care of her, even when things get really hard and scary. It is a slow burn that feels very real, showing you the side of love that is not about flowers and dates, but about staying by someone's side when they can no longer help themselves.

The acting here is some of the best you will ever see because it feels like you are watching real people, not actors. The movie does not move fast, and some parts might feel a bit heavy or sad, but that is what makes it hit home. If you want a story that makes you think about family and aging, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: As Anne gets worse and loses her ability to speak or move, she begs Georges to help her end her life. Georges tries to be strong, but eventually, he can't watch her suffer anymore. In a heartbreaking final act, he smothers her with a pillow to let her go. He then seals their bedroom door with tape to shut out the world, staying with her one last time before the story closes.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves powerful stories about true love and sacrifice.
